Yirandhali may, according to Robert Dixon, belong to the Maric branch of the Pama–Nyungan language family. According to Peter Sutton, the list of words given by an early settler, M. Armstrong, of the language of the Upper Cape River, which Norman Tindale ascribes to the Yilba, actually refers to the Yirandhali language. What did the Yirandhali believe about yarrabi? According to Christison, the Yirandhali believed the landscape was also occupied by spirits (yarrabi), the most feared of which was one, Koonkoolmujja, who haunted the rocky areas. Another kind, Korribberum, would roam the downs, scrambling along on four legs, but hospitable to those whom he might encounter. What are some popular Country Songs in Australia? Popular Australian country songs include "Click Go the Shears" (Traditional), "Lights on the Hill" (1973), "I Honestly Love You" (1974), "True Blue" (1981), and "Not Pretty Enough" (2002). Children's music in Australia developed gradually over the latter half of the 20th century.
